title: F172 - Lesson 9: Gene Therapy - Viral & Non-Viral Vector Delivery
courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology - Unit F172: Genetics
focus: Gene Therapy: Viral & Non-Viral Vector Delivery Systems, Tropism, Packaging Limits, and Anatomical Barriers
deliverable: OCR AAQ Level 3 Human Biology (Unit F172: Genetics) Lesson 9 presentation covering in vivo, ex vivo, and in situ delivery routes, viral vectors (AAV serotypes, Lentivirus, Adenovirus), non-viral systems (Lipid Nanoparticles, electroporation, hydrodynamic delivery), and convection-enhanced delivery across the blood-brain barrier.

objectives.knowledge: Differentiate the structural biology, genome packaging capacities, and chromosomal integration profiles of AAV, lentiviral, and adenoviral vectors.
objectives.application: Evaluate non-viral nanotechnologies (ionizable lipid nanoparticles, cellular endosomal escape) alongside physical permeabilization techniques for therapeutic delivery.
objectives.evaluation: Select and justify the optimal delivery vector for specific clinical phenotypes (e.g. adult non-dividing neuronal vs dividing hematopoietic stem cells).

terminology.def: Single-stranded DNA parvovirus (4.7 kb packaging limit) maintaining long-term episomal expression in non-dividing cells without host integration.
Recombinant retrovirus accommodating 8-10 kb payloads that permanently integrates into host chromosomal DNA, transmissible across cell division.
Non-viral spherical nanocarriers composed of ionizable cationic lipids, helper lipids, and PEG-lipids enabling nucleic acid encapsulation and endosomal escape.
Positive-pressure bulk flow microinfusion through intracranial cannulae driving macromolecular therapeutics through brain tissue.

slides.title: F172 Lesson 9: Gene Therapy Vector Delivery
slides.subtitle: OCR AAQ Level 3 Human Biology · Unit F172: Genetics (Dan)
keyTakeaways: Comprehensive coverage of viral vectors, non-viral systems, and delivery barriers.
Direct preparation for understanding delivery strategies in clinical practice.

slides.title: Foundations of Gene Delivery: In Vivo, Ex Vivo & In Situ
slides.subtitle: Anatomical administration routes and therapeutic compartmentalization
keyTakeaways: In vivo delivers vectors systemically or locally directly to patient tissues.
Ex vivo harvests, genetically engineers, and reinfuses patient cells (e.g. HSCs, CAR-T).
In situ applies targeted microinfusion to isolated organs (e.g. striatum, subretinal space).

slides.title: Adeno-Associated Virus (AAV): The CNS Gold Standard
slides.subtitle: Tropism, episomal safety, and 4.7 kb genetic payload constraints
keyTakeaways: AAV2, AAV5, AAV9 display high tropism for non-dividing neurons and photoreceptors.
Remains non-integrating episomes, eliminating insertional oncogenesis risk.
Strict 4.7 kb packaging limit requires compact cDNA or miRNA expression cassettes.

slides.title: Lentiviral & Retroviral Vectors: Permanent Integration
slides.subtitle: Host chromosome insertion, dividing cell utility, and oncogenesis risks
keyTakeaways: Permanently integrates transgenes into dividing host lineages (hematopoietic stem cells).
Accommodates larger genomic payloads (8–10 kb).
Carries insertional mutagenesis risk if inserted near proto-oncogenes.

slides.title: Adenoviral Vectors & Alternative Viral Platforms
slides.subtitle: High payload capacity, transient expression, and acute immunogenicity
keyTakeaways: Adenovirus vectors carry up to 30 kb but provoke intense innate inflammatory clearance.
Transient expression makes adenoviral platforms ideal for vaccines rather than chronic cure.
Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) provides natural neurotropism with massive payload capacity.

slides.title: Lipid Nanoparticles (LNPs): Non-Viral Nanotechnology
slides.subtitle: Ionizable lipids, endosomal proton sponge effect, and cellular escape
keyTakeaways: Ionizable cationic lipids are neutral at pH 7.4 and positively charged in acidic endosomes.
Disrupts endosomal membrane, releasing therapeutic mRNA or sgRNA into cytoplasm.
Lack of viral capsids permits repeatable systemic dosing without neutralizing antibodies.

slides.title: Physical Delivery Modalities: Direct Membrane Entry
slides.subtitle: Electroporation, microinjection, and hydrodynamic delivery
keyTakeaways: Electroporation uses high-voltage microsecond pulses to induce transient aqueous membrane pores.
Microinjection offers single-cell precision for zygotes and early embryos in transgenics.
Hydrodynamic high-pressure infusion permeabilizes capillary endothelia in targeted organs.

slides.title: Overcoming Anatomical Barriers: The Blood-Brain Barrier
slides.subtitle: Endothelial tight junctions and stereotactic Convection-Enhanced Delivery
keyTakeaways: Brain capillary endothelial tight junctions block >98% of systemic macromolecules.
Stereotactic Convection-Enhanced Delivery (CED) bypasses BBB via positive-pressure microcannulae.
Ensures homogeneous distribution across deep brain nuclei such as the caudate and putamen.

slides.title: Comparative Vector Selection Matrix
slides.subtitle: Evaluating payload size, dividing status, integration, and immunogenicity
keyTakeaways: AAV: 4.7 kb payload, non-dividing cells, episomal, low immunogenicity, years of expression.
Lentivirus: 8-10 kb payload, dividing cells, integrated, moderate immunogenicity, permanent.
LNPs: Flexible cargo, non-integrating, low-moderate immunogenicity, transient expression.

slides.title: Lesson 9 Formative Knowledge Check & Exam Scenario
slides.subtitle: Retinal gene therapy vector selection and clinical justification
keyTakeaways: Justify AAV selection for adult retinal dystrophy based on post-mitotic tropism.
Explain why non-integrating episomal expression is safe and durable in non-dividing tissues.
